title: Build the governed AI tool, then own it.
summary: Seven weekend-length courses where learners build a working, governed AI system they control, with no coding background required.
audience: Learners and teams ready to build a bounded AI system.

collection.heading: Choose a governed system to build and own.

methodology: Derive membership from resource kind and path
Link directly to the current course route
limitations: Collection membership reflects published canonical resources

title: The twelve lessons that make you dangerous with AI.
summary: Twelve practical lessons covering foundations, prompting, trust, safety, getting started, and everyday work skills.
audience: Individuals and teams developing practical generative-AI fluency.

collection.heading: Choose the lesson that matches the work in front of you.

limitations: Lessons cannot cover every tool, jurisdiction, or organizational policy

title: Step-by-step builds you can finish this week.
summary: Six self-contained playbooks for lead generation, client intake, content repurposing, knowledge bases, SOPs, and governance.
audience: Operators who need a practical workflow rather than a conceptual overview.

collection.heading: Choose a workflow and leave with a working first version.

assumptions: Users test playbooks with representative work
limitations: Workflows require adaptation and accountable owners

title: Copy-and-use prompts, policies, and docs.
summary: Free editable prompt packs, policies, roadmaps, and worksheets for strategy, operations, marketing, and governance.
audience: Learners and teams who need a reusable starting document.
assumptions: Users adapt and review templates before use
limitations: Templates are not organization-specific professional advice

title: Clear, honest guides to the tools worth your time.
summary: Evidence-first guides to what AI tools are good at, where they fall short, and how to assemble a stack that fits the work.
audience: Individuals and teams comparing AI tools without affiliate-driven recommendations.

collection.heading: Choose by workflow, evidence, and constraints.

methodology: Separate vendor claims from observed behavior
assumptions: Users verify current pricing, terms, and policies
limitations: Tool capabilities and commercial terms change

title: See what AI actually does for a business like yours.
summary: Use cases organized by job and business context, each connected to the lessons, templates, and playbooks that make the work concrete.
audience: Leaders and practitioners translating general AI capability into a specific business function.

collection.heading: Start with the job that needs to be done.

methodology: Connect use cases to implementation and guardrails
assumptions: Users validate fit against their actual work
limitations: Examples do not establish organizational or regulatory suitability

title: When you want a partner, here is how we work.
summary: Six service pathways for strategy, workflow design, implementation, governance, team training, and ongoing fractional AI leadership.
audience: Teams moving from free learning into scoped implementation support.

collection.heading: Choose the smallest engagement that resolves the current constraint.

methodology: Make scope and fit inspectable before contact
assumptions: An engagement is scoped before work begins
limitations: Pricing, timing, and availability depend on scope
